newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Thousands stranded as Sri Lanka ships halt service.
newsitem.headline: Thousands stranded as Sri Lanka ships halt service.

text.p: Thousands of refugees were stranded in Sri Lanka after shipping companies cancelled services to the northern Jaffna peninsula following attacks on two ships by Tamil Tiger separatists, aid officials said on Friday.

They said refugees from the northern rebel-held Wanni region were waiting in northwestern Mannar and eastern Trincomalee for ships to take them to Jaffna, but shipping lines were scared to move without naval escort.

"There are at least 3,800 people in Mannar and another 3,000 in Trincomalee. More are likely to come to Mannar. But there are no ships to take them back," said an aid official who declined to be identified.

Shipping firms halted services following attacks on two ships by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
The rebels attacked and torched a refugee ship near Mannar last week before taking away its crew of nine, including two Indonesians. Only the crew was on board.
Earlier this week they hijacked a North Korean vessel which had carried food to Jaffna and killed one crew member. The remaining 37 are still being held.
The rebels said in the statement on Thursday that they had captured the North Korean ship as it "was sailing within Tamil Eelam's territorial waters".
Aid officials said at least five other ships hired by government agencies to ferry food and refugees to the north had halted operations after the attacks.
Government officials in government-held Vavuniya, some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, said shipping lines were demanding naval escort before starting their service again.
Military spokesman Brigadier Sarath Munasinghe said on Thursday that security forces would solve the problem, but added it was not possible for the navy to escort all civilian ships.
